title: Stakeholder heatmap and automated notification rules for cross-surface release trains
creator: Liam O'Connor
description:
Problem: As we scale simultaneous launches across runtime, console, and API surfaces, ad-hoc email threads and manual Slack pings are causing coordination gaps during critical windows (canaries, capacity hedges, regional blackouts). We need a lightweight operational artifact and automation layer: a stakeholder heatmap that surfaces who needs to know about which signal (latency SLO breaches, capacity pressure, rollout health) and an automated notification ruleset that ties those signals to specific channels, cadence, and escalation steps.

Goal: Produce a living stakeholder heatmap integrated into the launch calendar + a rule-driven notification engine (workflows) that triggers notifications based on telemetry and schedule state. This should reduce noisy alerts, speed decision handoffs during launches, and make ownership clear across runtime, console, and API teams.

Scope: Build a product-management owned heatmap template and a set of notification rule templates. Integrations: PagerDuty (escalation), Slack (channels per lane), Email (for exec summaries), Launch Calendar (read/write tags), and Runtime/Console telemetry dashboards (links). Out of scope for MVP: full incident automation; deep on-call routing (will rely on existing PagerDuty configs).
acceptance_criteria: Stakeholder heatmap template created and stored in Confluence with mapping for common launch signals (canary failures, latency SLO > 3x, capacity throttling, rollout aborts).

Notification ruleset v1 defined as a JSON/YAML spec and implemented in the launch-runbook automation for at least three signals: canary-failure, regional-capacity-plateau, and pre-launch blackout violation.

Automated notifications successfully sent in a staging rehearsal: Slack channel ping (lane-specific), PagerDuty trigger for P0 escalation, and daily email summary for execs during the staged release window.
Heatmap and ruleset reviewed and approved by Runtime, Console, API, and GTM leads; signoff recorded in the launch runbook page.
Documentation includes clear handoff steps and rollback criteria tied to each notification rule.

notes: Design trade-offs: MVP will prioritize clarity of ownership over full automation — initial rules will be conservative (no automatic rollbacks).
Risk: If telemetry canonicalization is delayed, rehearsals will use a mapped shim which could miss edge cases. Contingency: manual verification step pre-rehearsal.
Success metrics: reduce cross-team Slack coordination messages during launch windows by 40% (measured via thread count), reduce mean time to decision for canary failures from 22m to <10m.
Follow-up: after MVP, evaluate 2-way integrations (allow teams to acknowledge/clear notifications from Slack and write back to the launch calendar state).
